newsitem.title: BRAZIL: MOTOR RACING-CRASH FORCES RE-START OF BRAZIL GP.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-CRASH FORCES RE-START OF BRAZIL GP.

text.p: The Brazilian Grand Prix was halted on the opening lap on Sunday after a multiple collision at the first corner.
It re-started without incident a short time later.
In the first start, Canadian Jacques Villeneuve, in a Williams, appeared to be forced wide by German Michael Schumacher's Ferrari as they went into the opening bend.

Villeneuve had started from pole position but was unable to take advantage and careered wide across the gravel track through the downhill Senna curve where he was followed by four other cars as the field started the race.
Italian Giancarlo Fisichella in a Jordan spun on the opening bend, causing chaos among the following cars, including the Arrows of world champion Damon Hill.
Brazilian Rubens Barrichello, in a Stewart, appeared to hit Fisichella's Jordan while Hill's car suffered front wing damage.
German Heinz-Harald Frentzen was also forced to take an unscheduled excursion across the gravel trap and grass while Dane Jan Magnussen, in a Stewart, was left stranded after stalling on the grid.
In the re-start, Schmacher led at the first bend but was overtaken by Villeneuve after one lap.
